defects.description: match() re-scans the whole rule list for every record, so a 100-record batch performs 10000 probes against the stated 200-operation budget instead of resolving each record through one indexed lookup of the rules.

trigger.input: import { RuleMatcher } from "./src/matcher.js"; const counter = { count: 0 }; const rules = []; for (let i = 0; i < 99; i++) rules.push({ region: "r" + i, channel: "web", route: "route-" + i }); rules.push({ region: "eu", channel: "web", route: "route-eu" }); const records = []; for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) records.push({ region: "eu", channel: "web" }); const matcher = new RuleMatcher(rules, counter); const matched = matcher.matchAll(records); console.log(counter.count + " probes, " + matched.filter((m) => m !== null).length + " records routed");

defects.why_missed: The suite asserts only which rule each record matches and that the injected counter moves, never how many probes a full batch performs, so a linear rescan per record reads as correct output.
